The British press (The Times, The Economist) systematically pushed
a narrative to justify their tacit support for the South:
1. Economic Grievance: The war is a mere tariff dispute over
the North's 1861 Morrill Tariff.
2. Lust for Sovereignty: The North is fighting merely to
forcefully subjugate 8 million Anglo-Saxons.
3. Irrelevance of Slavery: The institution of slavery has
absolutely nothing to do with this war.
Marx notes a fatal flaw in this logic: the protectionist
Morrill tariff passed after the rebellion broke out.
Secession caused the tariff, not the other way around.

Diplomatic Crisis: Emotion vs. International Law
The British Press Outrage
Established Maritime Law
Claims the US flagrantly violated neutral
shipping rights by searching a British
vessel and kidnapping highly
respectable passengers.
The Right of Search: Adopted fully by
the US from British precedent.
• Contraband: Queen Victoria's own

court), not a material violation of international law. The pretext for war was a legal quibble.

The Military Stalemate
By late 1861, over a million men face
each other across a front from Missouri
to the Chesapeake Bay. Yet, months
pass with endless marching and
counter-marching without a single
decisive action.
Engels' Observation
Two unwieldy bodies of men, each
afraid of the other, and almost
as afraid of victory as of
defeat. The system of warfare is
completely barren. Why?
